translation.english_text: Tch... tch... tch...
Now tell me... how precious are honour and valour... can we allow them to be trampled under the enemy's feet?
No!... No!
Then unite under my leadership to free Pazhuthar.
Brother! This younger brother is always ready to serve under your leadership...

Ready.

I'm ready.

I'm ready too.

I'm ready too....

source_locator.description: Velazhagan arrives laughing.

translation.english_text: [Velazhagan arrives laughing.]

Everyone is ready... but I am the one who is not ready... Let you freedom fighters out, eh?... Slaves! Sitting in the mouth of a mountain python, are you blowing the magudi of freedom?... I'll throw you right into its belly... Look... can you see the prison that is going to torture you?...
notes: `மகுடி` is retained as `magudi`, the reed-pipe image paired by the source with the mountain-python metaphor.

translation.english_text: Prison!... You don't understand revolutionary poetry!... Know this... a flower grove where the mango-cuckoo sings... the prison that thinks to trap us...
notes: The poetic source fragment is translated as printed and is not externally attributed or expanded.

translation.english_text: Don't talk back... shut your mouth!......

source_locator.description: Velazhagan drags Muthan and pushes him inside.

translation.english_text: [He drags Muthan and pushes him inside.]

source_locator.description: After Velazhagan pushes Muthan inside, the unlabelled threat continues from the same speaker.

translation.english_text: You insects of Pazhuthar! Worms!... You trip the tiger—beware;... say 'hm' and it's prison; ask 'why' and it's exile!
notes: This is the closed source-context-attributed `ammaiyappan-s030-r001`; no printed speaker label is invented.
The antithesis `'இம்' என்றால் சிறைவாசம்; 'ஏன்' என்றால் வனவாசம்` is preserved as `say 'hm' ... ask 'why'`.

source_locator.description: Velazhagan leaves quickly.

translation.english_text: [He leaves quickly.]

source_locator.description: Vedalam and Sukhadev are present.

translation.english_text: [Vedalam and Sukhadev are present.]

Vedalam! As you told me, I have finished all the arrangements. I have spent two thousand gold coins... jewels... clothes, this and that... bought everything... Will my Muthayi come?... Vedalam... this Kannagi Mansion is waiting for my beloved... will that maiden come?...
notes: Source `கண்ணுடி` is rendered contextually as an affectionate `beloved`; the Tamil form is not changed.

translation.english_text: (Holding them apart) Certainly, brother!... Touch one of the two! (He touches one.)
notes: Both source-owned parenthetical actions remain inside the immutable dialogue unit.

translation.english_text: Ah!... She will definitely come, brother...
Will she come?...
All right!... Name a flower, brother!...
A flower!... This one? Tamarind blossom...
Why all this fuss!... I will go myself and bring Muthayi... You stay right here... I will be back at once.

source_locator.description: Muthan is freed by his friends, whispers a secret to them, is recaptured by hidden Vengaiyur soldiers and dragged to Velazhagan.

translation.english_text: [Muthan is in prison. His friends stealthily come and free him. He whispers a secret into their ears and leaves. Vengaiyur soldiers who have been watching from hiding spring on him and seize him, then immediately drag him to Velazhagan.]
What?...
Vedalam has come...
Vedalam?... Tell him to come, tell him to come...
Come in, Vedalam... I assume you have come with victory...
Only the beginning of victory, my lord!—our new quarry is caught by a brand-new hunter!
notes: The source's hunting metaphor is retained without attempting to normalize the compact phrase `புது புதிய வேடனிடம்`.

translation.english_text: What?... what?...
I will tell you... Sukhadev and Muthayi—their wedding is at Kannagi Mansion in Anandapuram...
I arranged it myself...
(Angrily) What?...
Come now... I began this plot only to deliver Muthayi to you...
Explain it so I can understand...

You must do exactly as I say... Sukhadev and Muthayi are going to be married... You must send Muthan there immediately... If Muthan goes, Muthayi will run away with him... While the two of them are escaping, we will drive Muthan off and abduct Muthayi alone...
Good plan... What if Muthan understands our plot?...
Hm... In the intoxication of love he will not think about anything... a horseman comes in.
notes: The source-owned arrival cue remains inside this immutable Vedalam dialogue record.

translation.english_text: My lord! Muthan escaped from prison... We have caught him and brought him back...
Where?... Bring him in... Vedalam, hide yourself for a while...

source_locator.description: Muthan is dragged in.

translation.english_text: [Muthan is dragged in.]

All right! You may go... hee... hee... hee... Mutha!... Even if you had not escaped from prison, I was already thinking of releasing you myself... good young man!... I have put you through a great deal... I am sorry for that....
Sir! You have suddenly changed... How did you realize that I am without refuge?...... Even a god could not have come and told you!

A human being has something called conscience. When a man becomes a beast, that conscience turns into a worm and lies subdued. When beastliness is defeated, the wormlike conscience rises as a spotted peacock and dances... It is in that dance that the beauty of truth begins to shine.

english_page_segments.english_text: A human being has something called conscience. When a man becomes a beast, that

conscience turns into a worm and lies subdued. When beastliness is defeated, the wormlike conscience rises as a spotted peacock and dances... It is in that dance that the beauty of truth begins to shine.

translation.english_text: Ah! A splendid thought sprouts even here, like a red lotus sprouting from mud...
Mutha! Do you know what news opened my eyes?... That Sukhadev is going to force your beloved Muthayi into marriage...
Really?...

Yes! The wedding is at Kannagi Mansion in Anandapuram... Run before her life leaves her... Mutha! You may wonder why I suddenly care so much... You have read the story of Layla-Majnun, have you not?... There is not much difference between this and the episode in which Layla's husband sent her back to her lover Qays... Mutha, let me tell you one thing... you and Muthayi may live as a family under my protection... but why worry about that now?...... Go at once... save your life-companion... [goes inside and returns with fine clothes] Here! Run this instant... regain your lost love... here are fine clothes. Put them on... go and complete your wedding happily!...
notes: The Layla-Majnun/Qays reference is translated only as printed; no external narrative detail is imported.
Frozen `இஞ்ஞுனே` is handled contextually as a deictic urging interjection; the Tamil source remains unchanged.
The bracketed clothes-fetching action remains inside the immutable source dialogue record.

translation.english_text: I am deeply grateful to you, sir...

source_locator.description: Muthan rushes away, hears laughter and watches from hiding.

translation.english_text: [He rushes away. Then he hears laughter and watches from hiding.]
Bravo, my lord! You played it very well.

The fellow was thoroughly fooled...

Vedalam!... What is the next arrangement?...
The next arrangement!... Send five or six horsemen under my command. I will return with that beauty.
I will give you a thousand gold coins... if you come back with her...
[To himself] They are plotting.... I will turn that plot to my advantage.
notes: The source-owned `[தனியாக]` aside remains inside the immutable dialogue unit.

translation.english_text: Comrades! Thanapathi is using me as a tool to abduct Muthayi. I will use this opportunity and disappear.
Then what will become of us, anna?
You too, somehow escape from here and come to me. Then all of us together will work for Pazhuthar's liberation. Vāṭṭamā nāṉ?
notes: Frozen source `வாட்டமா நான்?` is retained by transliteration rather than silently repaired or guessed from context.

translation.english_text: Go carefully, anna! We will somehow come and join you.—We must get out by cunning.
Father, why is no one here? Where is he, father?...
Oh, oh! In such a hurry already? Once the leaf is laid out, would they fail to serve the rice? Come, girl, come......
notes: The meal-leaf/rice metaphor is preserved as source rhetoric.

translation.english_text: Yes... all the arrangements for the wedding...

Are you looking around thinking there are no drums, no wedding pavilion, no feast?... This is only the bride's house. The muhurtham will take place elsewhere. Besides... this wedding has to happen without Sukhadev knowing about it...
notes: `முகூர்த்தம்` is retained as `muhurtham` for the ritual wedding moment.

translation.english_text: Yes.... yes... that Sukhadev...

source_locator.description: Tirisangu sees Sukhadev arriving.

translation.english_text: [Tirisangu sees Sukhadev arriving.]

source_locator.description: After seeing Sukhadev arrive, Tirisangu turns the interrupted description into a face-saving remark to Muthayi.

translation.english_text: You say he is very handsome—someone you like very much......
notes: The source prints no speaker label for this line; Tirisangu attribution remains derivative provenance only.

translation.english_text: Father... what are you babbling about!...

source_locator.description: Muthayi turns, sees Sukhadev and faints.

translation.english_text: [She turns, sees Sukhadev and faints.]
What?... what?...
Nothing... nothing... The shock of seeing you made her faint... the heart pounds from happiness, does it not, brother?...
notes: Frozen spacing in `ஒன்றுமில்ல ை` is not treated as a source correction.

translation.english_text: Yes!... yes! Mine too is pounding just like that now...
All right; you go upstairs. I will come later.

source_locator.description: Sukhadev leaves; Muthayi recovers and Tirisangu displays costly jewels and clothes.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev leaves. Muthayi recovers from her faint and rises. Tirisangu shows her costly jewels and clothes.]
Muthayi! Look at these... ornaments set with pearls, coral, gems and diamonds! Shining silk!... glittering diamond! Precious gem! Ah... ha... all these....
A price that pleases your heart! A net cast over your daughter!...
notes: Frozen `தாப்படும்` is rendered from the immediate price/net contrast without changing the Tamil source.

translation.english_text: Listen to what I say...

Do not say anything. I understand everything now. The very shell brings the pearl and drops it in the mud!... The red-lotus creeper itself plucks off its petals and gives them to the buffalo! Father, would you plot like this against your own daughter?!...

english_page_segments.english_text: Do not say anything. I understand everything now. The very shell brings the pearl and drops it in the mud
!... The red-lotus creeper itself plucks off its petals and gives them to the buffalo! Father, would you plot like this against your own daughter?!...

notes: The immutable source record prints speaker label `திரி`, even though the rhetoric addresses `அப்பா`; English preserves the record ownership and does not relabel the Tamil evidence.

translation.english_text: Daughter!... If you were a daughter, would you let a father's heart burn like this? If you were truly a daughter—an aged father—a loving father—a man who has suffered many days in poverty—now thinks he might finally live a little, would you not think of helping him?... To let me live, am I asking you to jump into a fire? Am I asking for some great sacrifice?.... A position impossible to find... he says he will place you there and worship you as its goddess... yet you sob, heave and lament, foolish girl! I have fulfilled so many wishes of yours; can you not fulfil this first and last wish of mine?....
Many times I have given you tender coconuts; what difference is there, father, between what you are saying and a coconut tree saying, 'Just once, I will fall on your head'?...
notes: The coconut-tree analogy and its reversal of parent-child obligation are preserved literally.

translation.english_text: Tch, insolent chatterbox! Keep quiet! In the morning you and the prince are to be married!... Get yourself ready for it...

source_locator.description: Tirisangu leaves quickly and sees Vedalam outside.

translation.english_text: [He leaves quickly. As he comes outside, he sees Vedalam.]
Come... you have arrived at a good time...
What, Tirisangu? How are all my arrangements......
All the arrangements are fine! There is just one flaw.
What is it?
Muthayi refuses to marry Sukhadev...
That's a fine thing! It is like saying the meal is ready but there is no rice! What, man... earlier you said the two of them were lovers united as one...
notes: Frozen spacing in `இல்ல ை` is not normalized in the Tamil evidence.

translation.english_text: Muthayi is a stubborn girl. I cannot change her obstinacy... You must somehow...
Hm... I will try... Where is she now?
She is inside.
All right, all of you come; I will set her right myself!...
notes: Frozen `நீங்கள் யாரும் வாருங்கள்` is translated without silently changing the source despite the following action showing Vedalam entering alone.

source_locator.description: Vedalam goes inside and addresses Muthayi.

translation.english_text: [Vedalam goes inside. Seeing Muthayi, he speaks.]

Foolish girl! Get up! Why are you sitting like this?... Won't you speak?... Hm... this is exactly the time that is slipping away... the sea is roaring... and you are sitting on a catamaran singing an oppari!... Ah! Look to what must be done, dear girl! Crying cannot ward off danger...... Why are you crying?
notes: `ஒப்பாரி` is retained as `oppari`, a lament form.
The frozen phrase around `தகப்பன் இது தான் நேரம் போவிருக்கிறது` is translated conservatively from immediate context and is not repaired in Tamil.

translation.english_text: The town laughs; I cry...
True. Yet, tender-hearted maiden! Realize that there is still a chance to escape this turmoil...
A chance to escape!...
Yes... a chance indeed... your liberation... the sign that your suffering is departing has come in the form of Vedalam...
What are you saying?....

You do not know how affectionately Muthan and I have lived as friends... the gold you gave, Sumathi swallowed and kept... Muthan was locked in the camp prison... I gave the wealth I had saved with great hardship over many days and have now freed him.

english_page_segments.english_text: You do not know how affectionately Muthan and I have lived as friends... the gold you gave, Sumathi swallowed and kept... Muthan was locked in the camp prison... I gave the wealth I had saved with great hardship over many days
and have now freed him.

notes: Frozen source `பொண்ணு` is interpreted from the immediate money plot as the gold/money Muthayi had sent; the Tamil evidence is not changed.

translation.english_text: Ah!... Has my Muthan been freed?

Alas, pitiable girl!... Hear more happy news. I came to know that your father is cruel and arranged this marriage by deceiving you... so I ran here at once to save you!... I have come like a wedding guest, trying to free my friend's beloved.
Sir! May you live for many years!
Why should I live long in this unjust world, girl? Never mind that... Listen, young bird!... Muthan will come here tonight; leave with him.
Will he come?...
Would he fail to come?... Be careful, both of you!

source_locator.description: Vedalam leaves and Muthan enters the room disguised as an old man.

translation.english_text: [Vedalam leaves. Muthan enters the room disguised as an old man.]
Aththan! Vedalam said you would come.
notes: `அத்தான்` is retained as `Aththan`, the intimate kinship/address term used by Muthayi for Muthan.

translation.english_text: Vedalam! He is a venomous snake! Muthayi, somehow you must make Sukhadev come here.
notes: Exact source label `முத்` is preserved; context identifies this speech as Muthan without rewriting the label.

translation.english_text: Sukhadev? Why?
notes: Exact source label `முத்` is preserved; context identifies this reply as Muthayi.

translation.english_text: Do you know why? For us to leave now is no ordinary matter; danger is waiting all around us!
notes: Exact source label `முத்` is preserved; context identifies this speech as Muthan.

source_locator.description: Tirisangu comes in and Muthan hides.

translation.english_text: [Tirisangu comes in. Muthan hides.]
Muthayi! Still not asleep?...
I cannot sleep, father!... I am deep in thought.
What are you thinking about, girl?...
That Vedalam came and put sense into me... all these days I had lost my wits and trusted that Muthan...
My daughter! Is it really you speaking?... Ah! Vedalam was right... Muthayi, only now do I feel I have gained the benefit of having you as my daughter...
Father, will you do me a favour?...
I will do a thousand; tell me!
In the morning Sukhadev and I are to be married. Now I want to meet him and speak about a few things! My heart too is longing to see him...
My darling daughter!... Is that such a great matter? I will send him right now...

source_locator.description: Tirisangu leaves quickly; Muthan whispers the plan to Muthayi and leaves.

translation.english_text: [Tirisangu leaves quickly. Muthan tells Muthayi the secret plan and leaves.]

source_locator.description: Tirisangu goes to Sukhadev and tells him of Muthayi's eagerness.

translation.english_text: [Tirisangu goes to Sukhadev and tells him of Muthayi's eagerness.]

Ah! My goddess of love! Here I come. Can fire and cotton remain still when brought close together? Uncle! You can go and sleep soundly—I will not let Muthayi sleep tonight—I am going to keep talking to her!...
notes: The fire/cotton erotic metaphor is preserved rather than euphemized.

source_locator.description: Sukhadev comes to where Muthayi is.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev comes to where Muthayi is.]
My dear! Why did you call me? Oh! Won't you speak? Are you this shy?...
I need to discuss something.
Discuss something? A lover and beloved—this bedchamber is a pavilion of sensual delight, not a place for discussing news, my dear!...
notes: The source's sexual innuendo is translated without euphemizing it.

translation.english_text: You must not make all these jokes...
What do you want to talk about? Speak!...
What is your opinion about equality between men and women?
Half man—half woman—my principle is that men and women should be created as Ardhanarishvaras themselves—if I were God, that is exactly how I would make them!...
notes: `அர்த்தநாரீஸ்வரர்கள்` is retained as `Ardhanarishvaras`, preserving the source's religious image rather than replacing it with an abstract equality term.

translation.english_text: Ah... you have stated a vast and complicated matter so briefly!... The woman fortunate enough to attain you is lucky indeed—I want to ask one more thing.
notes: Frozen spacing in `உங்களேஅடை யும்` is not used to alter the Tamil source.

translation.english_text: Do not ask all these things retail—ask wholesale!
notes: The `சில்லறை` / `மொத்தமாக` retail/wholesale wordplay is preserved.

translation.english_text: If I ask it, you cannot answer immediately. We have to talk for a long time.
We will talk—never mind—what other pleasure do I have except talking with you!
What a lovely moon—shall the two of us go toward the riverbank and talk of pleasant stories?
notes: Frozen `சுவையான க்கதைகள்` is translated contextually without changing the Tamil record.

translation.english_text: Ah!... You have said the long thing—come, let us set out, my dear!...
notes: Frozen `நீண்டதைச் சொன்னாய்` is retained semantically close to its printed form rather than silently normalized to a more expected phrase.

translation.english_text: Shh... do not touch... all that is for tomorrow! Come, let us go...
I am ready...
You say men and women are equal—then you in women's clothes, and I in men's...
Oh no, in women's clothes?
See! Being a woman means degradation...
No... no... it is not that; I would feel shy if the men saw me...
We are going secretly so no one will know, are we not? When you and I are one life in two bodies, what is wrong in your wearing my clothes and my wearing yours?...

english_page_segments.english_text: We are going secretly so no one will know, are we not? When you and I are one life in two bodies, what is wrong in your wearing my clothes and my
wearing yours?...

translation.english_text: There is nothing wrong, my golden treasure! I will do exactly as you say...

source_locator.description: Sukhadev appears in women's clothes and Muthayi in men's clothes; Velazhagan's soldiers are hidden nearby.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev appears in women's clothes and Muthayi in men's clothes. Velazhagan's soldiers are hidden nearby.]
My jewel, Muthayi! What a sweet moment!... What a wonderful sight!... Ah! To have you beside me... alas, I do not even understand where we are going!...
You will not understand... you will not!... You... must come without speaking.

source_locator.description: The soldiers mistake Sukhadev for Muthayi, attack and carry him away; Muthayi remains, and Muthan comes from behind and startles her.

translation.english_text: [The soldiers mistake Sukhadev for Muthayi, attack him and carry him away. Muthayi remains. Muthan comes up from behind and startles her.]
Hey! Who is that?...

source_locator.description: Muthan and Muthayi laugh together.

translation.english_text: [They both laugh.]
So—that is done. What is our next plan?
The next plan? Give me your ring like this... up... put it on the finger!... Here!... stretch out your finger...
notes: `கணையாழி` is rendered as `ring` from the exchange-of-rings action that follows.

source_locator.description: Muthan puts his ring on Muthayi's finger.

translation.english_text: [He puts his ring on her finger.]
What is this?...
When two lovers are of one mind, exchanging rings itself is marriage...
All right... we are married now... what next?...
From now on... f... f... we have to run a family...
notes: The source stammer `கு...கு...குடும்பம்` is retained through an English stammer rather than smoothed away.

translation.english_text: Run a family right here in the forest?...

Why not?... Did Rama and Sita not live in the forest for fourteen years? When a man and woman are alone, there is no dwelling more delightful than forest-dwelling... Look at the peacock dancing in joy! Look at the cuckoo singing melody to the ear's fill! Look at the river!—look at the waterfall!—look at its beauty!—come a little nearer and look!

english_page_segments.english_text: Why not?... Did Rama and Sita not live in the forest for fourteen years? When a man and woman are alone, there is no dwelling more delightful than forest-dwelling
... Look at the peacock dancing in joy! Look at the cuckoo singing melody to the ear's fill! Look at the river!—look at the waterfall!—look at its beauty!—come a little nearer and look!

notes: The repeated `வாசம்` in the forest-dwelling line carries wordplay that cannot be reproduced exactly in English; the residence sense is preserved.

translation.english_text: Hm...
Rama must have spoken to Sita like that... Would forest life have been bitter for them?... It may have been bitter for Lakshmana... poor man, married yet a brahmachari!
notes: `பிரமச்சாரி` is retained as `brahmachari` to preserve the comic cultural reference.

translation.english_text: Mischief!
All right, Muthayi, come! We must live hidden in disguise... otherwise Velazhagan will somehow catch us... come... come!...

Muthayi! Am I the only one waiting for you?... Look, even the moonlight in that sky is waiting... Angry girl! Maiden of cool speech! Why have you still not come?... Are those horsemen blockheads?... Or are these steeds themselves unable to understand my urgency? How long... how long... I told them then itself... that a shortcut should be laid between Anandapuram and the capital... If this foolish king had listened, how quickly my Muthayi could have arrived by now!...
notes: The source's repeated waiting/urgency rhetoric is preserved rather than smoothed away.

source_locator.description: Soldiers bring Sukhadev dressed as a woman.

translation.english_text: [The soldiers bring Sukhadev dressed as a woman.]
Muthayi! You've come?... Muthayi, won't you speak?... Ah! Who has closed those lips that pour out golden words?... These horsemen are fools!

source_locator.description: The gag is removed; Sukhadev cries out and Velazhagan becomes angry.

translation.english_text: [The gag is removed. Sukhadev cries out, and Velazhagan grows angry.]
Sir, my lord! Don't hit me...
How did you come here?...

Muthayi and I—she as a woman and I as a man... no... no... she as a man... I as a woman... we put on disguises and went to the riverbank to play happily... and then, my lord, this danger befell me!...
Fool! Get out of here without telling anyone outside...
notes: Exact source label `தன` is retained; downstream character identity must not rewrite the printed label.

source_locator.description: A proclamation is beaten on the drum; Muthan and Muthayi enter in disguise.

translation.english_text: [A proclamation is beaten out on the drum. Muthan and Muthayi enter in disguise.]
notes: The intervening source `* * *` is structural and is not translated as prose.

translation.english_text: This is to inform everyone that... a man named Muthan has escaped from the Vengai-country army... His identifying marks are—a budding moustache—a handsome young man—a ruddy complexion—a bronze voice—whoever catches and hands him over will receive a proper reward!... This is the order of Velazhagar, commander of Vengai country!... Dum!... dum!...

source_locator.description: Muthan and Muthayi approach a merchant's house; the merchant is with a child.

translation.english_text: [Muthan and Muthayi come toward a merchant's house. The merchant is with a child.]

See that, little one! Dum... duma... duma... will you catch the runaway and hand him over?...... [The child cries.] Hey!... don't cry... lovely sight... sacred ornament of a beautiful gem-studded mansion... an indelible painting... a dancing golden lamp... aararo...
notes: The child-cry cue is embedded inside this immutable dialogue record and stays there.

`ஆராரோ` is retained as the source-visible lullaby-like vocable. The closed song/performance inventory does not retain this span as a separate occurrence, so no song unit or authorship claim is created.

source_locator.description: Muthan and Muthayi are seen approaching.

translation.english_text: [Muthan and Muthayi are seen approaching.]
Who? Who... are you? What do you want? I can't give you any alms... I have an infant to care for...
notes: Exact source label `தன` is preserved. In this record the closed record-aware character layer resolves it to the merchant role; that identity aid does not rewrite the Tamil label.

translation.english_text: We're looking for some kind of work...
Have brother and younger sister set out together?.......
Oh no!... we're husband and wife, master...
Hmm... what work can you do?...
We'll do whatever work we're given without refusing. He isn't well... only I...
All right... can you raise this child?...
Do you have experience?...
Even the child is reaching for me... come here, little one!......

The child has no mother—has come into the world, as the source puts it, like a banana bunch... you must look after it... there are no wages... just food for the two of you... here is a thatched hut... you can live in it...
notes: Frozen spacing in `வாழைக்குல ைமாதிரி` is not silently repaired. The unusual banana-bunch simile is retained conservatively rather than normalized away.

translation.english_text: All right...
What's your name?...
My name is Ponni... and he...
Mm... don't say your husband's name... poor thing... my name is Ponnan, master!
notes: The disguise names Ponni/Ponnan are source-visible and are not normalized into character aliases.

translation.english_text: Hmm... two young birds—blossoming flowers—where have you gone to sing your love-song? Tirisangu! Don't worry. You have found a Manmatha fit for your daughter. Now let her sing her song—and him his!
notes: The source plays on `பாடு` after `காதல் கீதம்`; English keeps the song/plight echo as far as possible.

translation.english_text: It was not because he was a Manmatha that I got tangled up in all this trouble and arranged this marriage. I, who lie in a leaky hut......
notes: Frozen `பொல்லாம் கட்டப்பட்டு` is rendered from the immediate context without altering the Tamil source.

translation.english_text: You thought you could stroll on an upper storey as the Palayakkarar's relative by marriage—that is it, isn't it! What of it now—Sukhadev and Muthayi will soon return after finishing their romantic tour.

english_page_segments.english_text: You thought you could stroll on an upper storey as the Palayakkarar's relative by marriage—that is it, isn't it! What of it
now—Sukhadev and Muthayi will soon return after finishing their romantic tour.

translation.english_text: When? When I am on my way to the cremation ground?

So what if it is then? The grandson who will light your funeral pyre will be a future Palayakkarar, won't he? Hee... hee... hee... Tirisangu! Leave all that. I gave you the idea for such a magnificent wedding arrangement—where is my reward?
notes: The funeral-pyre joke and `Palayakkarar` social title are preserved.

translation.english_text: Reward?
Shall I call it wages?
Do not play with my pain.
Play? This Vedalam does not play, Tirisangu... The reward you owe me must come, respectfully. Otherwise......
Otherwise what will you do?
What will I do? I will tell the Palayakkarar that you deceived Sukhadev and ruined him. Be careful!
Do not frighten me. The Palayakkarar is not a fool who will simply believe your unsupported lie.
No proof? The fact that Muthayi is not in your house is itself strong proof for me, do you understand?
Enough! Stop! You were the one who gave the idea too.
That will not help you in this case, man! Wait... wait, I will deal with you. If you behave properly, you will survive. Otherwise.....
Otherwise—I will die. That is all, isn't it! Do not threaten me. Do whatever you can.
Tirisangu! That fellow! He acted like a good man and carried out a jackal's trick—the traitor!
notes: Frozen `வாட்டும் அவன்` is handled contextually; the Tamil source is not repaired.

translation.english_text: It is the good people one must not trust in these times, my lord.

Who's there? (A servant enters.) Go at once, bind Tirisangu hand and foot, and drag him here. No matter how much wealth is lost—only bring my son back to me. If he does not return, the queen will die.
notes: The servant-arrival action remains inside the immutable source dialogue record.

translation.english_text: No one should learn that Sukhadev is missing. I myself will find him by stratagem and bring him back to you.
Thank you very much. I will give you five hundred gold coins—if Sukhadev is found, I will give you five hundred gold coins as a reward. Wait here—I will be back.

source_locator.description: Baladevar leaves.

translation.english_text: [Baladevar leaves.]

They say sorrow comes with company and happiness comes alone—that is wrong! Is happiness not marching upon Vedalam like a line of ants? Hmm... one man can seek comfort only by striking another! The fly is food for the spider—the spider is food for the lizard—the lizard is food for the cat—the cat is food for the Kuravan—the Kuravan is food for Yama—that is my path too! At the speed of my rise, perhaps I may even become the Palayakkarar of Pazhuthar!...
notes: The source's predatory food-chain rhetoric is preserved. `குறவன்` is retained as `Kuravan`, a source social/community label, without euphemistic substitution; `எமன்` is rendered as Yama.

translation.english_text: (Coming back from inside) Vedalam! Here, take this!
notes: The return/action remains inside the immutable dialogue record.

translation.english_text: Most honoured lord! I will somehow bring your precious son back. May the Lord be my aid! Ammaiyappa!

source_locator.description: Muthan is talking with his friends while Muthayi watches from a crack in the doorway.

translation.english_text: [Muthan is talking with his friends. Muthayi stands at a crack in the doorway and watches.]

Pazhuthar must win freedom somehow... This thought must take root in the people's hearts... If the feeling of liberation spreads like wildfire, then in a single day we can raise the flag of freedom in Pazhuthar and drive out Vengai country's domination!
If we are to change the people's minds...
Thinking alone will not do... we must act...
Yes... that is my opinion too...
Wherever the people direct their attention, we must spread our ideas through every such sphere...
Ah!... what anna says is right!...
notes: Exact source label `தோழ 2` and frozen spacing in `அண்ண ாசொல்வது` remain unchanged in provenance.

translation.english_text: You go... I will come after attending to the rest...

source_locator.description: The friends leave; Muthayi enters.

translation.english_text: [They leave. Muthayi enters.]
Muthayi...!
Yes; what is all this?
The beginning of the liberation struggle! They are my comrades... I am gathering an entire force like this so that Pazhuthar may be liberated...
I am afraid...
Foolish girl! Afraid?... Purananuru will laugh at you!...
notes: The source only invokes Purananuru rhetorically; no external poem or passage is imported.

translation.english_text: If you wage a liberation struggle and your life is put in danger...
What else—will they lay a feast for a freedom fighter?... Look here... even this child keeps looking at me... Hey!... if only we had one like this....
Wait another eight or nine months...
notes: The source statement is translated directly; no explanatory pregnancy prose is added.

translation.english_text: Ah... is that so? You did not tell me...

source_locator.description: Young ascetic Sukhadev is in nishta with a `Muthayi` japa when Vedalam enters disguised as an ascetic.

translation.english_text: [Young ascetic Sukhadev sits in nishta, performing japa of “Muthayi.” Vedalam enters disguised as an ascetic.]
notes: The booklet explicitly marks this as a character japa/performance cue, not a soundtrack song. `japa` and `nishta` are retained as source religious-practice terms; no lyric or authorship is inferred.

translation.english_text: Om Shakti! Chamundi, Mahakali, Parameswari, Renukamba, Sundari, Soundari, Niranthari, Duranthari, O Uma who stands as radiance!.... You remove the suffering of those who behold and worship sukha varttiyinai!... Ambike! Jagadambike! Kali!...
notes: The invocation preserves the printed goddess-name sequence. Frozen `சுக வார்த்தியினைக்` is not silently repaired; `sukha varttiyinai` is retained transliteratively where the source sense is uncertain.

source_locator.description: Vedalam looks at Sukhadev.

translation.english_text: [He looks at Sukhadev.]
Muthayi... Muthayi...
notes: This labelled spoken japa token is the dialogue-layer span linked to `ammaiyappan-song-004`; the separate japa unit owns only the preceding performance cue.

translation.english_text: Young ascetic! First, my greetings...
White-bearded elder!... The world is false! What do you want?...
In this false world, a true jnani!... What place are you from?... Looking at you, it seems as though you have lost something that captured your heart!...
notes: Frozen `இஞ்ஞானி` is rendered contextually as `jnani` without changing the Tamil evidence.

translation.english_text: Ha... ha... ha! You are an extraordinary man! How did you see what was in my heart? How did you reveal it? Are you the sage who knows the three times—Devarishi Narada himself?...
notes: The Narada reference is translated only as printed; no external narrative detail is added.

translation.english_text: Brother!... My eye of wisdom tells me that you are a man defeated in love... Is that true?...
Yes! How do you know?...
For the virtuous, every corner of the world is visible... You are a palace-dweller!... Through the enchantment of a woman, you have become an ashram-dweller! Isn't that so?...
notes: Exact source label `வே` is preserved. `ஆணங்கு` is rendered from the immediate romantic context without altering the Tamil source.

translation.english_text: Yes, Swami! They say only those who have escaped the enchantment of women can become ashram-dwellers... I myself have been bound by that enchantment and become a mendicant!...

Nothing surprising... Viswamitra left the palace and came to the ashram... Even there, the trouble from beauties did not leave him... he, a very summit of the greatness of penance... the child Menaka bore...
notes: The Viswamitra–Menaka reference is translated only to the extent printed; the elliptical source wording is not externally completed.

translation.english_text: Ah! Most excellent ascetic, rich in ripened experience and abundant devotion! Through you alone I seek the end I desire. Grant me the boon...
notes: Frozen `தன் பயனை` is rendered from the immediate boon-seeking context without an upstream Tamil correction.

translation.english_text: I understand! You want to attain that four-letter maiden... that is all, isn't it?...
Mu—th—tha—yi! Ah!... taccu... taccu... You said it exactly right, true guru!... That jewel of a woman's name has only four letters!...
notes: The source's frozen `தச்சு...தச்சு...` is retained as `taccu... taccu...` rather than guessed into a normalized expression; the printed four-letter joke is preserved.

translation.english_text: I will arrange your marriage with her... You do not need this guise at such a young age!... Do all that must be done in worldly life first, and in the years when age no longer lets you go on, say ‘Siva, Siva’—that is the proper course for human beings...
notes: Frozen `செய்யவேண்டிய அகமெல்லாம்` is handled from the immediate worldly-life/renunciation contrast without changing the source.

translation.english_text: Will I get my Muthayi?... My god who came to me without my seeking!... Just as Narada came between Murugan and Valli, you have come between Muthayi and me—my father blessed with the Lord's divine grace! Praise!... praise!...
notes: The Murugan–Valli–Narada reference is translated only as printed.

translation.english_text: All right, come... let us go to my place... You will have Muthayi soon...

source_locator.description: Muthayi takes the merchant's child to the seashore; a storm and heavy rain break; a tree falls and traps Muthayi while the child is separated.

translation.english_text: [Muthayi takes the merchant's child to the seashore. A storm rises. Heavy rain pours down. She comes running with the child!... A swaying tree breaks. Muthayi is trapped beneath the fallen tree. The child is separated and left alone.]

english_page_segments.english_text: [Muthayi takes the merchant's child to the seashore. A storm rises. Heavy
rain pours down. She comes running with the child!... A swaying tree breaks. Muthayi is trapped beneath the fallen tree. The child is separated and left alone.]

source_locator.description: The storm has subsided; Vedalam and Sukhadev are seated in a mandapam.

translation.english_text: [The storm has subsided. Vedalam and Sukhadev are seated in a mandapam.]
Some phantom came upon the woman, seized her to devour her... casting a spell over her eyes...
notes: The source line is elliptical and chant-like; English follows its immediate printed sense without creating a separate verse or song unit.

source_locator.description: The merchant enters.

translation.english_text: [The merchant enters.]
Sir... sir! Did you see a woman and a child, sir?...
What! A woman and a child?... There are so many men and so many women on the seashore...
No, sir! As usual, the maid came to the seashore carrying my child...
notes: Frozen spacing in `இல்ல ை` is not treated as an upstream Tamil correction.

translation.english_text: Go... go... go and search!

source_locator.description: The merchant leaves.

translation.english_text: [The merchant leaves.]
Seems what we're searching for itself can't be found. And now this fellow too... Come, swami, let's go.

source_locator.description: The merchant comes searching for the child, finds the child crying beneath a tree and picks the child up.

translation.english_text: [The merchant comes searching for the child. He finds the child standing beneath a tree and crying, and picks the child up.]
God!... You saved me. You saved this poor man...
notes: Exact source label `தன` is preserved in provenance; English does not rewrite the immutable label from character resolution.

source_locator.description: Muthayi lies unconscious beneath the tree; Sumathi passes that way and sees her.

translation.english_text: [Muthayi lies unconscious beneath the tree. Sumathi comes that way and sees her.]
Who is that?... Alas, poor thing! [She looks.] Ah!... Muthayi... Muthayi...
notes: The source-owned parenthetical `(பார்க்கிறாள்)` remains inside this immutable dialogue unit rather than being split into a separate stage unit.

source_locator.description: Sumathi embraces/supports Muthayi and leads her away.

translation.english_text: [She supports Muthayi in her arms and leads her away.]
Where is Ponni?
If I had not gone, that would have been the end of the child. A tree branch broke in the wind and fell...
Where is Ponni?
Oh! In my haste I forgot her!
notes: Exact source label `தன` is preserved rather than normalized to the longer merchant label.

translation.english_text: You forgot her! It is not only poor people like us; your class of lords has long since forgotten one virtue of the compassionate heart.
notes: The source's class accusation in `சீமான் இனம்` is preserved rather than softened or modernized.

source_locator.description: Muthan runs out.

translation.english_text: [Muthan runs out.]

source_locator.description: Muthayi enters Sumathi's house with her; Vedalam and Sukhadev see them.

translation.english_text: [Muthayi enters Sumathi's house with her. Vedalam and Sukhadev see them.]
They are going into this house... Swami, shall we go too?...
Wait, my son!
I'm waiting...
Come... come... let us go back to our place... We now know where Muthayi is. It is my duty now to unite her with the man she ought to join...
Fulfil that duty quickly, Swami!
So be it... all right... all right... come...
That day, without understanding you, I spoke angrily. Forgive me...
Let us forget all that!
After your marriage, where did all your mischievous talk run off and hide?...
It has not hidden anywhere... Let him regain his health... then listen to me talk! Muthayi, you call my speech kurumbu—mischief; do you know what he calls it?... karumbu—sugarcane!
notes: The source wordplay `குறும்பு` / `கரும்பு` is retained through transliteration plus gloss because the sound contrast carries the joke.

translation.english_text: Hmm, all right, all right... do not keep talking only about your man... pay a little attention to mine too...
notes: Frozen source wording `என்னுடைய வரையும்` is rendered from the immediate contrast without altering the Tamil evidence.

source_locator.description: Sukhadev knocks at the door while Vedalam is inside speaking with the commander.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev knocks at the door. Inside, Vedalam is talking with the commander.]
Swami! Swami!
Wait. My nishta is not over yet.
notes: `நிஷ்டை` is retained as `nishta`, the source's ascetic/meditative term.

translation.english_text: Sukhadev has come, Swami! Open the door.
Blind devotee! Wait. I am talking with God—about Muthayi...
(To himself) Aha! Is he talking with God? We cannot see Bhagavan ourselves. Sinful soul that I am! At least while the Swami speaks, let me hide and watch!
notes: The source-owned `(தனக்குள்)` cue remains inside the immutable dialogue record.

source_locator.description: Sukhadev opens the window shutter, looks inside and is badly startled.

translation.english_text: [He opens the window shutter and looks inside. He is badly startled.]
Ah! Ayyo! The commander!... Vedalam is climbing the drumstick tree again. Appa! Good thing—I escaped... (He runs.)
notes: The source proverb-like image `வேதாளம் மறுபடியும் முருங்க மரம் ஏறுகிறது` is preserved literally rather than replaced by an English idiom.
The printed `(ஓடுகிறான்.)` action remains inside the immutable dialogue record.

translation.english_text: It seems the escaped Muthan too is gathering a liberation force and plotting to free Pazhuthar. Like two mangoes with one stone, we must catch that fellow Muthan as well.
notes: Frozen source spacing in `சேர்த்து க்கொண்டு` is not repaired in the Tamil evidence.

translation.english_text: Let that be, Vedalam! Why talk pointlessly to me now about a liberation force when I am wandering in search of where my pleasure lies? First bring that beautiful-bodied woman somehow!
notes: `சுகம்` is kept in its immediate sense of pleasure/comfort; the source's wording can also resonate with the name Sukhadev, but English does not force an identification.
Frozen `வீணுக` is rendered contextually as `pointlessly` without changing the Tamil source.

translation.english_text: Wait. I will return victorious.

source_locator.description: Muthayi is lying down; Vedalam calls out.

translation.english_text: [Muthayi is lying down. Vedalam calls out.]
Amma!... Amma!...
Who are you, sir?... What do you want?...
Who here is Muthayi?
Why!... What is it?
Muthan has been attacked by enemies and is in a dying condition.
notes: `மரணவஸ்தை` is translated directly as a dying condition; English does not add medical detail.

translation.english_text: Ah!... Aththan!...
notes: `அத்தான்` is retained as `Aththan` because the kinship/lover address matters to the scene's register.

translation.english_text: Are you Muthayi? If you come with me, you can see him alive...
Sir!... Where is he? Take me to him...
All right, come; I will show you.

source_locator.description: Sukhadev arrives and sees Muthayi leaving with Vedalam.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev arrives there and sees Muthayi leaving with Vedalam.]

source_locator.description: After arriving Sukhadev sees Muthayi leave with Vedalam, the unlabelled monologue is his reaction.

translation.english_text: Aha! Is this villain the one taking my beloved away? Unarmed as I am, how can I take direct action?... Hmm... we shall see...
notes: The source prints no speaker label for this monologue; Sukhadev attribution remains derivative provenance only and is not promoted into a printed label.

translation.english_text: I abandoned my beloved in pitch darkness and am crying out. How will I rescue you... my precious beloved! He came in the guise of a holy man and tricked me! Muthayi! Muthayi! How will I rescue you from that brute?...

source_locator.description: Muthan passes that way.

translation.english_text: [Muthan passes that way.]

Hey, Mutha! Stop—stop—you came at just the right time! There is no time now to ask where you are, how you are, and all that... Vedalam, dressed as an ascetic, has deceived my dearest beloved Muthayi and is taking her somewhere.

english_page_segments.english_text: Hey, Mutha! Stop—stop—you came at just the right time! There is no time now to ask where you are—how you are—
and all that... Vedalam, dressed as an ascetic, has deceived my dearest beloved Muthayi and is taking her somewhere.

translation.english_text: Ah! Where?
He must have gone to his rest-house...

source_locator.description: A covered figure is inside; Vedalam arrives with Muthayi.

translation.english_text: [Inside, a figure is covered with a blanket... Vedalam arrives with Muthayi.]
There... your beloved!

source_locator.description: Muthayi pulls away the blanket calling Aththan; Velazhagan rises.

translation.english_text: [Eagerly crying 'Aththan,' she pulls away the blanket. Velazhagan rises.]
Muthayi!... Full moon!... you've fallen into my hands?... You called 'Aththan'; that is not dear Muthan, but Commander Velazhagan! Do you recognize me?...
notes: `அத்தான்` is retained as `Aththan` because the kinship/lover address matters to the scene's register.

translation.english_text: Commander Velazhagan! You, who ought to protect the country, have become a wanderer like this... No. I am your sister...
Only fools would believe that the flower and the bee are brother and sister, dear!...

source_locator.description: Velazhagan grabs Muthayi's hand.

translation.english_text: [He grabs her hand.]
Fie!... Let go of me! Shameless man!... Poisonous storm! I am not a tree that will topple in the cyclone of your lust...
Scold me! Scold me well! Every letter tastes sweet... A caged parrot cries not from anger!... from fear! Even that will become normal with habit...
Don't come near me!...
The commander of this country's army calls you... Do you know what happens to those who do not obey my command?...
You'll kill me! That's all, isn't it?... I won't fear death! Is death more terrible than you? No... no... never!
Muthayi!—No flower has ever escaped from my iron-like arms!... Remember that!...
Let me go, you wrongdoer!...

The whole world turns on the axle called injustice!... Muthayi!... You can no longer escape... Yield of your own accord!... [He comes closer—Muthayi tries to run.] Where are you running? Wherever you go, I will not let you go... If you fly as a skylark, I will become the hawk circling you!... If you leap as a spotted deer, I will roar as a tiger! Even if at last you become a corpse, I will become the sandalwood log that touches your body and burns with it! My delight!... Yield... fragrant new blossom flowering in spring! Come to me. Coloured lotus! Bouquet of dazzling flowers!... I will sweep you into my powerful arms... Leap upon me, green parrot!...
notes: The source-owned parenthetical approach/escape cue remains inside this immutable dialogue record. The coercive rhetoric is translated as printed and is not euphemized.

translation.english_text: Do not ruin yourself in vain; stand away...

[With a terrifying laugh.] Now no one will come forward to offer you refuge by destroying me!... You've read in stories: the beloved is in danger... the hero runs in and saves her! None of that will happen here!... Even that Sita could not be easily rescued from Ashoka Vanam by the divine-incarnate Ramachandra Murthi! Remember! Pitiful woman!... Someone has taught you that you must conduct yourself with chastity like Kannagi!... That was the age of the Silappathikaram... literature that ought to be banned... a philosophy this army commander cannot permit... O maiden! Come near...
notes: The parenthetical terrifying laugh remains dialogue-owned. Sita, Ashoka Vanam, Ramachandra Murthi, Kannagi and Silappathikaram are translated only as printed references; no external narrative is added.

translation.english_text: Warrior who bears spear and sword in battle! Do not behave so cowardly toward a woman...
Shall I behave heroically then?...
Let me go...
Even fruit that comes to the hand—a bird that comes within sight—people will not let go! Muthayi! I warn you; don't test my patience......

source_locator.description: Velazhagan approaches to embrace Muthayi.

translation.english_text: [He comes near to embrace her.]
Fie! [She slaps him.]
notes: The slap is printed inside the immutable dialogue record and remains dialogue-owned.

source_locator.description: Velazhagan draws his sword; Muthan jumps down from above.

translation.english_text: [He draws his sword. Muthan jumps down from above.]
Mutha!... Don't die in vain! Think carefully about who your enemy is...
notes: Frozen source syntax in `நீ யார் என் பகை நிதானித்துக் கொள்` is rendered only by the immediate threat sense; the Tamil is not repaired.

translation.english_text: Me? I am the warrior who was trapped and ruined in the `kāppāri` of your arbitrary rule—in the hall of dictatorship!... But today that warrior has not come... I have come to reward you for the blood I shed—for the tortures I endured—I have come to reward you, man, reward you! Madman who hunts women! Liquor and the pleasures of women may hide in the shadow of your delusion... but you are intoxicated madmen who cannot realize that a revolutionary force will surge up and smash that delusion to dust...
notes: Frozen `காப்பாரியிலே` is retained by transliteration as `kāppāri`; its exact lexical force is not silently repaired from context.

translation.english_text: Don't forget whom you're talking to, Mutha!
I am playing with you, who are playing with my life!
notes: Frozen spacing in `உன் னோடு` is not repaired upstream.

translation.english_text: If I move my forefinger, you'll be smashed to pieces...

Ha, ha!... Will your pointing finger shoot me?—No... smash me to pieces... The age in which you lived by intimidation is over, Commander! Now an age of rationalism is coming, making room for people of character alone to live. You are my enemy. Keep your longbow... The seats of power of those who, like you, sped along in the footprints of dictatorship have become hollows and mounds, then graveyards with no trace of where they once stood!
notes: The frozen clusters `சுட்டு தியுமா`, `என்ன கண்ணைப் பார்த்திராமா` and `நீளவில்வைத்துக் கொள்ளும்` are irregular. English follows only the immediately recoverable rhetorical sense and does not claim a Tamil repair.

english_page_segments.english_text: Ha, ha!... Will your pointing finger shoot me?—No... smash me to pieces... The age in which you lived by intimidation

is over, Commander! Now an age of rationalism is coming, making room for people of character alone to live. You are my enemy. Keep your longbow... The seats of power of those who, like you, sped along in the footprints of dictatorship have become hollows and mounds, then graveyards with no trace of where they once stood!

translation.english_text: Do you know what is in my hand?...

I know very well... What is the glitter of a knife in a coward's hand before the roughness of a warrior's palm? You have a knife!... Here is my weapon! A weapon forged in the camp of Duty, Dignity and Discipline! A weapon that stands against scoundrels—knife-thrusts—dishonourable acts!...
notes: `கடமை, கண்ணியம், கட்டுப்பாடு` is rendered as the source's rhetorical triad `Duty, Dignity and Discipline`.

translation.english_text: Such a great warrior?... A warrior who will face a knife bare-handed?... Here, let us see that too...

source_locator.description: Muthan and Velazhagan fight; Kurumban sees it and runs; Velazhagan dies.

translation.english_text: [The two fight fiercely. Kurumban arrives. Seeing the situation, he runs away. The fight ends with the commander's death.]
Aththan!...
notes: `அத்தான்` is retained as `Aththan` because the kinship/lover address matters to the scene's register.

translation.english_text: Muthayi!...

source_locator.description: Kurumban arrives with soldiers.

translation.english_text: [Kurumban arrives with soldiers.]
Ah!... Commander!... Ayyo, are you dead? Hey, carry him away. Hey Mutha! You killed him, didn't you?... Hey, arrest this fellow too.

source_locator.description: Soldiers fight Muthan; he is captured; Muthayi cries out and faints.

translation.english_text: [The soldiers fight Muthan. In the end Muthan is captured... Muthayi cries out and faints.]

source_locator.description: The commander's corpse is carried away; Sukhadev sees it.

translation.english_text: [They carry away the commander's corpse. Sukhadev sees it.]

source_locator.description: Muthan is dragged in.

translation.english_text: [Muthan is dragged in.]
Hey, Mutha! You killed the commander?... Bravo, bravo... thank you... thank you... Where is Vedalam? Didn't he die?...

source_locator.description: Sukhadev goes inside.

translation.english_text: [He goes inside.]
Ah!... Muthayi!... Muthayi!... Open your eyes and look... the warrior Sukhadev has come... Open your eyes and look, Muthayi! Get up...
[Coming out of her faint.] Are you the grove criminal?
notes: The parenthetical recovery from fainting is printed inside the immutable dialogue record and remains dialogue-owned. `சோலைக் குற்றவாளி` is translated literally from the frozen source phrase.

translation.english_text: I am no criminal... that Muthan is the criminal!
Ayyo, my god of love! In your hands...
It's nothing... only a water cup, dear... Don't be afraid, dear... get up...
Sinner! So you alone have come?...
Why are you angry, Muthayi? Is this some lovers' sulking?...
notes: `ஊடல்` is rendered as lovers' sulking/quarrel, preserving the intimate register rather than flattening it to generic anger.

translation.english_text: What are you saying now?
What else would I say? About our marriage, of course!
You scoundrel!... You have come to speak a heroic epic to me while I stand at the edge of agony? Is this the lesson they taught you in your palace? Go... get out! Hmm, are you going or not?...
Uh-uh... no one is going anywhere... Muthayi, do you know who I am? The son of the future emperor!
The emperor's son! Hmm... you have no eyes... no human feeling... They say a woman's reproach is terrible. Haven't you read that?...
notes: `பெண் பழி பொல்லாது` is rendered as the source's warning that a woman's reproach/curse is dangerous; no external proverb text is imported.

translation.english_text: Hmm... why would I read all that... Muthayi, now you simply must marry me... dear Muthayi!...

Hmm... I am ready... It is this body you want, isn't it?... You were bewitched by the sheen of my body, weren't you?..... Hmm... feast your eyes on my beauty! Someone said: only the body was soiled; the heart was not. Not so with me... I am ready to lay my chastity at your feet... You donkey charging in lust! Rake my heart with your cruel claws!..... Hmm... don't delay! Plunder my life!... Shatter my resolve to pieces! Representative of fiends who think of women as objects of prostitution!... Why should I hesitate? Here I am ready! My corpse is speaking to you! My dead body calls you! Come... come... deceiver! Here I am—Muthayi—Muthan's wife—your `vellatti`!
notes: The speech's bitterly sarcastic sexual-violence rhetoric is translated without euphemism. Frozen `வெள்ளாட்டி` is retained as `vellatti` because its exact social/sexual nuance is not silently normalized.

translation.english_text: What? You are Muthan's wife?... Muthayi, forgive me!... Listening to your father's words, I became corrupted like this! Trusting household life, I went as far as the boundary of ascetic life! Muthayi! I had carried my love for you toward marriage. Dear sister! I will go right now and save your beloved.
notes: Frozen `திருமணப் பெட்டுக்கு கொண்டிருக்கிறேன்` is irregular; English follows only its immediate marriage-directed sense and does not claim an upstream Tamil repair.

source_locator.description: Vedalam sits in a ruined mandapam with one thousand gold coins.

translation.english_text: [Vedalam sits in a ruined mandapam with one thousand gold coins.]

I got a thousand gold coins! God! A thousand salutations to you... Somehow make me the Palaiyakkaran of Pazhuthar... a crore salutations to you! A thousand gold coins for bringing Muthayi... From now on we don't need this disguise... We are subjects to none; we fear Yama not!
notes: The printed `நாமார்க்கும் குடியல்லோம்: நமனை அஞ்சோம்!` line remains embedded in Vedalam's immutable dialogue. English translates only the printed line and does not create a new literary-verse or song occurrence.

source_locator.description: Sukhadev arrives, becomes enraged, pushes down a stone and kills Vedalam.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev arrives there. Enraged, he pushes down a stone from the mandapam and kills Vedalam.]
This is the end for the wrongdoer!... In this world, only the man who reforms survives!
Commander Velazhagan... has been killed... a great disgrace to Vengai Nadu! Not only did he desert the army, he also killed the commander... That sinner must not be spared! Hang him at once.
notes: `தூக்கிவிடுங்கள்` is rendered by its immediate punitive sense as `Hang him at once.`

translation.english_text: For some reason, I have begun to doubt whether Sukhadev will return. Fate can close even our eyes... Even if Sukhadev stood before us, that fate has the terrifying power to draw a curtain over our sight...

source_locator.description: Poongavanam enters while the swami is speaking.

translation.english_text: [Poongavanam enters as he speaks.]

Hmm... the explanation of fate has begun!... You trust the swami—the poor swami trusts fate—fate lives trusting the swami—if fate keeps turning round like a wheel, Sukhadev too must be wandering somewhere or other...
notes: Frozen `சுற்றிக் கொண்டேதானி` is rendered from the immediate circular/wandering joke without changing the Tamil evidence.

translation.english_text: Hasty women...
Yes, Swami! That is entirely... entirely true... I am hasty... hasty indeed...
Poongavanam, enough. Stop it.

source_locator.description: Sukhadev comes running in.

translation.english_text: [Sukhadev comes running in.]
Father... father...
You have come back, my treasure!...
There is no time to fondle me... Father... matters have gone too far...
What are you saying?
Only if you come can a life be saved!
What is it, Sukhadev?
A poor man is being taken to the gallows! Save him... They called him an enemy-country spy, charged him with murder, and sentenced him... Father, set out at once for the gate of Vengai Puram!...
notes: The source's stacked accusation—enemy-country spy plus murder charge—is preserved without adding procedural detail.

translation.english_text: Tell me the matter in detail...
They have sentenced Muthan to death by hanging!...

source_locator.description: Poongavanam cries out `Muthaa` and falls.

translation.english_text: [Poongavanam cries out, “Muthaa!” and falls.]
Aunt!...
Poongavanam!... Who is there? Go at once and bring Physician Boopathi!...

source_locator.description: Physician Boopathi arrives, examines Poongavanam and gives medicine.

translation.english_text: [Physician Boopathi arrives, examines Poongavanam, and gives her medicine.]
Do not be afraid!... It is only mental shock... nothing else! Prabhu, why did she suddenly faint like this?... Any shock news?...
notes: The printed code-switch `ஷாக் செய்தி` is kept visibly as `shock news` rather than silently formalized.

translation.english_text: Nothing like that... You remember Muthan, Kaveri's son, who used to be the horseman in our mansion? It seems that Muthan has been sentenced to hanging! As soon as she heard that...

source_locator.description: Poongavanam again cries `Muthaa`; Boopathi begins thinking rapidly.

translation.english_text: [Poongavanam again cries out, “Muthaa!”... Boopathi's mind begins working rapidly.]
Prabhu! There are stairs behind this mansion, are there not?...
There are...

source_locator.description: Boopathi surveys the room and studies three paintings: love-pigeons, a cow seeking its calf, and a deer-skin Vengai image.

translation.english_text: [Boopathi surveys the room carefully. He studies the three paintings—love-pigeons, a cow seeking its calf, and the deer-skin Vengai.]
notes: The compact printed painting label `மான் தோல்வேங்கை` is kept source-bounded as `deer-skin Vengai`; English does not invent a more specific visual composition than the verified derivative states.

translation.english_text: Please take me to those rear stairs!

source_locator.description: They go; Boopathi counts the steps.

translation.english_text: [They go. Boopathi counts the steps.]

Aunt... aunt... do not worry, aunt! Good grief... Muthayi must be somewhere there worrying about Muthan too... Aha!... I came at such speed... and this physician has slowed even my speed down... Hmm... he has gone off to count steps—steps!... Come on, sir.
notes: The source's colloquial rhythm and repeated `படி` joke are retained rather than regularized into formal speech.

translation.english_text: What is it, Boopathi; why did you count the steps?...

I counted the steps—and with them I counted an old incident too... Aha! I remember it clearly—as though it were happening now, everything stands before my eyes exactly as a scene! I will tell that scene exactly. Listen carefully... One night this deceitful swami came running in haste and called me. There was a secret—he wanted it hidden. I came! He blindfolded me on the way. I refused. He gave me a sack of gold. I agreed. I did not know where he was taking me. My eyes remained bound. I could tell that I was being led up some steps... I counted the steps carefully. Thirty-six steps! I remember it well... In a dark room, amid dim light, my eyes were untied. To find out what place it was, I looked all around... These same three paintings were there even then!... A woman lay on a cot... her face was thoroughly covered with a black cloth... The woman writhed in labour pain. It seemed she might die in a little while... Then I treated her... Aha!... Aha!... a beautiful child—the swami immediately handed the child to a man named Kaveri. Kaveri ran away with the child. My eyes were bound again and I was brought back home. The very next day my journey abroad began. So that supreme secret lay buried in the underworld. Since I returned, I asked the swami any number of times; he would not tell me. But now I understand that this very room is where that child was born! Yes... this is the place where a cradle should have been hung for Muthan, who today stands at the gallows! But one thing, Prabhu! Why did this swami take so much care? I still do not understand...

source_locator.description: Poongavanam rises.

translation.english_text: [Poongavanam rises.]
I will tell you! I am Muthan's mother!
The one who deceived me is this very fiend here!

Anna! Forgive me! When you and anni had gone north, I fell into his net! This young ascetic used to come often, saying he would preach devotion... For one day—two days he spoke about the world. Then he explained the noble qualities of the creator of the world. He described even divine incarnations as having engaged in love-play. Maya Kannan—Manmathan—Rathi Devi—Mahesan, Parvati—Valli's bridegroom—Brahma, Tilottama—Menaka, Viswamithan—he told all these mythological tales—the intoxication in his words made my mind reel... Why describe it further—I fell... I fell... I fell from the path of chastity that the Tamil woman guards and protects... He said he would give up sanyasa and begin family life. At last Muthan came into my womb! Giving as his reason, ‘If I marry you, the town will clap its hands and laugh,’ he abandoned me! He is Muthan's father! I am the mother!

notes: The two-page confession remains one immutable dialogue unit.
The source's mythological-name sequence is translated only as printed; no external narrative is supplied. Frozen `விசுவாமித்தான்` is retained as `Viswamithan` rather than silently normalized.
`சந்நியாச சத்தை` is handled by its immediate renunciation/family-life contrast as `give up sanyasa`; the Tamil source is unchanged.

translation.english_text: Oh!... So this is the reason, aunt? Only now do I understand why you said you would not marry the king of Vengai Nadu!
Ha... ha... ha!... They say detached ascetics do not seek even revolution—you, however, have sought Poongavanam herself... ha... ha... ha!
notes: The repeated `நாடு`/seeking rhetoric is preserved as a joke culminating in Poongavanam's name.

translation.english_text: Boopathi! I will give you five thousand gold coins; do not tell this shameful news outside!...

I do not want five thousand gold coins! Because once before I became a slave to gold, this false masquerader was able to keep up his show for all these years!... Honourable Prabhu! There is no use hiding this secret any longer—go at once and save Muthan...
notes: `வெளிச்சம் போட` is rendered contextually as `keep up his show`; the verified Tamil remains unchanged.

translation.english_text: Comrades! We must free Muthannan somehow.
notes: `முத்தண்ணன்` is retained as the affectionate/respectful `Muthannan` rather than flattened to the bare name.

translation.english_text: I am ready to sacrifice even my life to rescue that warrior of ideals...
Even if we have to smash the gallows to dust, we will free Muthannan... Come!
Muthayi! Even after hearing all this, why do you say you will not speak to us?...
Do you think my deep sighs have no power to speak?...
My dear Muthayi!...
Do not touch me!
Are you the only one who worries about Muthan?... Do none of us worry?... To you he is a husband—to me, a son!...

Son! Do not say that once more... Your palace honour will be ground into dust. Shameless as you are, how can you call Muthan your son?... What a mother!... A mother who kept her mouth shut when her son was treated like a dog!... A mother who listened with relish to the news that her son was wasting away from hunger!... The very air of your palace drove you to hide the affection called son! Your false honour—status—respect—mannaangatti—everything!—stood in the way of calling him your child! Was it not because no blemish must fall on Palayakkarar pride that you treated the son you carried for ten months and bore as though he were a wanderer? Where is that arrogance now, mother? Have you come searching for your son because the curtain drawn over that arrogance has been torn away?... A mother who protects palace honour! A father who fans religious fanaticism!... The mother played the chaste wife!... The father danced the devotee!... Amma lived like an innocent maiden!... Appan lived out the devotee's evil deed! O Amma-Appars! Creatures of wretched character! New editions of fear itself! The woman who lost her chastity lived as a maiden—the lust-blinded man wandered as a swami! At the last moment, enlightenment has supposedly dawned on these embodiments of baseness!... Here come the shameless deceivers to inquire after one's sleep! Prestige must not be spoiled—even if the son is ruined, never mind, says the mother!... Public support must not decline—the name of son must not change—there is no concern for the son... yet these great good people have come to console their daughter-in-law! Shameless people—they danced, they sang, they enjoyed bliss, it seems—and once the emblem of that pleasure was born, like Viswamitra and Menaka they protected their empty prestige!—wretches!... The blessed souls who once threw that same veena into the ruins have now come to join its snapped string!... Leave this place; go away now! My Muthan is not here to answer all of you! If not today, tomorrow—not only to you but to worthies like you—a sword is growing in my womb to give the answer! A fire to devour false prestige!... A spear to destroy the mad elephants of religion that live by deceiving people is growing in my womb—it will answer the cheats!... answer the conspirators!... a fitting answer! a Self-Respect answer!... Wait for that answer, sinners!... Sinners who unjustly killed my Muthan! Wait for that answer—
